result.title: TIRAD: Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection
result.summary: Recent anomaly detection studies have shown that residual features, which model the discrepancy between normal and abnormal patterns, provide strong generalization to anomalies unseen during training. However, existing residual-based approaches mainly rely on visual discrepancies derived from image representations, while semantic discrepancies that can be explicitly expressed through language remain largely underexplored. To address this problem, we propose TIRAD, Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection, a multimodal residual learning framework that defines the discrepancy between textual representations of normal and abnormal states as a Text Residual Feature and uses it to guide the Image Residual Feature. Specifically, a Text Fusion Module converts patch-level text residuals into a gate that modulates the image residual of each patch. The gate retains the visual discrepancies that the text residual identifies as defect-related and attenuates the others, leading to more discriminative anomaly representations. Extensive experiments on industrial benchmarks and industrial-to-medical transfer demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing image-centric residual learning methods.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TIRAD，用「正常/异常」文本表示之差构造 Text Residual Feature，并转成 patch 级门控来调制图像残差特征，用于通用异常检测，在工业基准与工业到医学迁移上优于纯图像残差方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 文本语义门控逐 patch 筛选/衰减视觉残差的做法，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与视觉旁路设计提供借鉴；但该工作面向异常检测任务、不涉及推理期 latent 状态生成，其门控是否真正执行选择性证据保留仍需核查。
